text:
maria: quick sync: i'm proposing we split the intake path into a tiny triage-runner and a heavier bench-runner. triage-runner = sub-10s checks to unblock fast experiments. bench-runner = full quality/throughput suite. thoughts?
kevin: split makes sense. triage needs to be cheap and deterministic. what are the must-have checks?
san: must-haves: model fingerprint, tokenizer smoke, param count, single-forward sanity, and a small alloc probe for kv/cache. keep it under 15s.
julia: add an op-compat quick-scan: load graph and fail if unsupported ops appear. that avoids noisy converter errors later.
arun: operationally we should budget bench quotas. triage-runner is free, bench-runner consumes bench credits and goes to queue. also need a "fast-path" registry flag so internal experiments get auto-triaged.
meli: +1 on registry flag but call it `fast_path` to align with infra names. include owner/email for audits.
maria: agreed. for correctness comparators i suggest: top-k token overlap for next-token, logit-MSE with relative thresholds, and cosine on embeddings. surface breaches as warnings in triage but fail bench-runner if they exceed stricter thresholds.
kevin: can we keep golden artifacts tiny? maybe 16 canonical prompts per family and store trimmed logits/embeddings. bench-bot: bench-bot: created triage job `triage/5381239999` assigned to @eli, ETA 45m.
eli: i'll run the first triage. what command should i use?
arun: use `./triage/run_fast.sh --model-id=$ID --prompts=16 --kv-probe` — this spins a constrained container with memory caps.
san: on failures, auto-classify into taxonomy: TOKENIZER_FAIL, UNSUPPORTED_OP, OOM_PROBE, OUTPUT_MISMATCH, PERFORMANCE_ISSUE. map each to owner teams for automated issue creation.
julia: UI: triage view should show a compact histogram of token overlap and embed cosine, a tiny diff of shim changes, and a one-click re-run. also show historical triage passes for that model id.
maria: rollout gating idea: pass triage -> create shim & registry flag -> bench-runner queued -> canary (0.5% traffic, 1h) -> full rollout. if canary fails, auto-disable fast_path and route to fallback.
kevin: about the shim: make it minimal. a container that normalizes input dtypes/shapes and exposes quantization hints to runtime. we should version the shim and store it alongside model metadata.
eli: for golden comparisons, do we store raw logits? that's heavy. store top-20 logits plus embedding vector of 1024 dims maybe compressed.
san: compress embeddings with float16 and gzip. keep storage per-model < 1MB.
maria: metrics to assert automatically in triage: tokenizer_ok=true, forward_ok=true, kv_probe_ok=true, topk_overlap > 0.8 (for same-family), embed_cosine > 0.95. these are lenient; bench-runner has stricter cutoffs.
arun: i'll add `/v1/models/:id/triage` endpoint returning {status, quick_metrics[], artifacts_url}. bench-bot: bench-bot: job `triage/5381239999` completed: logs uploaded to gs://bench-artifacts/5381239999/logs.tar.gz.
eli: initial run: tokenizer edgecase found on one prompt (emoji tokenization). posting snippet below:
```
prompt: "I ❤️ Redwood"
model tokens: ["I", " ", "", "Red", "wood"]
expected: ["I", " ", "❤️", " ", "Redwood"]
```
kevin: emoji tokenization fails often on older tokenizers. mark as TOKENIZER_FAIL and route to tokenization team with sample.
san: automation: when TOKENIZER_FAIL, attach minimal reproducer + tokenizer config and run retry with updated vocab if provided.
julia: action items: 1) @arun add triage endpoint + registry flag. 2) @san produce 16-prompt canonical sets for 6 model families + tokenizer edgecases. 3) @eli run triage on the 3 pending models and attach logs. 4) @kevin add shim versioning to model registry. i'll mock the UI panels this week.
maria: thanks. goal: onboard experimental models in hours not days, while still catching the majority of blocker classes. we'll revisit thresholds after 25 models. :rocket:
